chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: What is the central purpose of OSHA process safety management?
options: Replace all occupational-health programs
Regulate only routine personal injuries
Eliminate the need for emergency planning
Prevent or minimize catastrophic releases of highly hazardous chemicals
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: PSM integrates process information, hazard analysis, operating discipline, integrity, change control, and learning to prevent major releases.
incorrectOptionExplanations: PSM is a process-risk system and does not replace other safety and health programs.
Its focus is catastrophic release prevention, not only personal injury statistics.
Emergency planning is one required supporting element, not something eliminated by PSM.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 38 and PSM homework; OSHA 1910.119 purpose and elements

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: A team begins a process hazard analysis without current chemical, technology, or equipment information. What should happen?
options: Complete and validate the process safety information needed to support the analysis
Continue and fill gaps after startup
Replace the PHA with employee interviews only
Assume original vendor data remain correct
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A meaningful PHA depends on accurate process safety information about hazards, process technology, and equipment.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Unknown design and hazard information can invalidate scenarios and safeguards.
Interviews are useful but cannot replace technical process information.
Changes, degradation, and documentation errors require verification.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: Which team composition best supports a PHA?
options: One manager with approval authority only
People with engineering and operations expertise, process knowledge, and knowledge of the selected analysis method
Only external auditors unfamiliar with the process
Only newly assigned operators
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The team must combine process knowledge, operating experience, engineering expertise, and competence in the analysis methodology.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Authority alone does not provide the multidisciplinary technical and operating knowledge needed.
External perspective may help, but process knowledge is essential.
Operators add valuable knowledge but cannot alone cover all required disciplines and method expertise.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 38 and PSM material; OSHA 1910.119(e)

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: A pump is replaced with a higher-capacity model that changes flow and pressure. How should the change be managed?
options: Treat it as replacement in kind because both items are pumps
Install it first and review only if an alarm occurs
Process it through management of change before implementation
Document it only in maintenance work history
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A change in equipment capability or process conditions is not replacement in kind and requires formal pre-change evaluation.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Replacement in kind requires equivalent design and function; changed capacity can affect process safety.
Post-installation review is too late to evaluate hazards and safeguards before exposure.
Maintenance history alone does not address technical basis, safety impact, procedures, and authorization.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 38, what constitutes a change; OSHA 1910.119(l)

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: Which item must be addressed before a covered process change is made?
options: Only purchase price and vendor delivery date
Only whether production supports the change
Only whether the new item fits physically
Technical basis, safety and health impact, procedure changes, duration, and authorization
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: MOC evaluates why the change is proposed, how it affects risk, what documents and training change, its duration, and who authorizes it.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Commercial information does not replace process-safety analysis.
Production support is not evidence that hazards and procedures are controlled.
Physical fit does not establish material compatibility, operating limits, or safeguard adequacy.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 38, MOC process, pp. 859-868; OSHA 1910.119(l)

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: A modified covered process is mechanically complete, but procedures and operator training are unfinished. Can startup proceed?
options: No; the pre-startup review must verify procedures and training are complete before introducing hazardous chemicals
Yes, if construction matches the drawing
Yes, if management accepts the schedule risk
Yes, if the first batch is smaller
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: PSSR confirms design conformity, procedure readiness, resolved PHA/MOC requirements, and training before startup.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Mechanical completion is only one PSSR element.
Management cannot waive fundamental startup readiness requirements.
A smaller batch can still expose workers and equipment to unreviewed conditions.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 38 and PSM material; OSHA 1910.119(i)

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: Inspection finds corrosion below the documented acceptable thickness on process piping. What is the strongest response?
options: Increase inspection interval to reduce disruption
Evaluate fitness for service and repair or replace the equipment before unsafe operation continues
Paint the pipe and close the finding
Rely on the absence of visible leakage
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Deficiencies outside acceptable limits require timely correction using recognized engineering and mechanical-integrity practices.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A longer interval increases time with a known integrity concern.
Coating does not restore wall thickness or pressure capacity.
No current leak does not establish acceptable remaining strength.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 38 and PSM material; OSHA 1910.119(j)

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: A process is routinely operated outside its written safe upper limit to meet demand. What should happen first?
options: Revise the limit after the shift without technical review
Keep operating because the deviation has become normal
Return to safe limits and investigate the deviation through the operating and change-control systems
Ask operators to monitor by smell
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Operating limits define safe conditions and consequences of deviation; recurring departures require control and formal evaluation.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Limits should not be changed without technical basis, risk review, authorization, and document updates.
Normalization does not make an analyzed limit irrelevant.
Odor is not a reliable or safe process-control method.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 38 and PSM material; OSHA 1910.119(f) and (l)

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: A contractor will perform turnaround work inside a covered process. Which host action is essential?
options: Transfer all process-safety responsibility to the contractor
Provide only a general site map
Wait for the contractor to request hazard information
Evaluate contractor safety performance and communicate process hazards, emergency provisions, and applicable safe-work practices
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: PSM contractor provisions require informed selection, hazard and emergency communication, safe-work coordination, and performance oversight.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The host retains specified duties for contractor selection, information, coordination, and oversight.
A map does not communicate process hazards and emergency controls.
Hazard communication and coordination must be proactive before exposure.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 38 and PSM homework; OSHA 1910.119(h)

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: Under OSHA PSM, when must an incident investigation be initiated after an incident that resulted in or could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release?
options: As promptly as possible, but no later than 48 hours
Within 7 calendar days
Within 30 days
Only after the regulator requests it
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: PSM requires prompt initiation, no later than 48 hours, to preserve evidence and begin learning from the event.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Seven days is associated with certain recordkeeping entries, not the PSM investigation start.
Thirty days delays preservation of evidence and exceeds the PSM initiation requirement.
The employer duty is triggered by the incident potential, not by a regulator request.

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: At what minimum frequency must an employer certify that it has evaluated compliance with OSHA PSM provisions?
options: Every month
At least every three years
Every five years
Only after a release
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: PSM requires a compliance audit at least every three years, with at least one knowledgeable person on the audit team.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Monthly auditing is not the stated minimum compliance-audit interval.
Five years exceeds the specified PSM interval.
Compliance evaluation is periodic and proactive, not only reactive.

questions.chapterTitle: Process Safety Management and Management of Change
questions.stem: A process has detection and shutdown systems but no coordinated response plan for a toxic release. What gap remains?
options: No gap because prevention makes response unnecessary
Only a financial reserve is missing
Emergency planning and response integrated with the process hazards and site arrangements
The process needs fewer alarms
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Process safety includes both prevention and preparation for credible releases through appropriate emergency action or response arrangements.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Prevention reduces likelihood but cannot guarantee that a release will never occur.
Financial planning does not provide notification, evacuation, response, or coordination.
Removing alarms would weaken detection and does not create a response capability.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
